headline: Why Your Custom Millwork Project Might Be Delayed
articleBody:
Planning custom millwork for your home in areas like San Marino or Pasadena is exciting, but sometimes things can slow down. One of the biggest culprits for delays is relying on initial architectural dimensions without verifying the actual site conditions. This sounds small, but if measurements are off, it can throw off the entire fabrication process. Another common snag happens when hardware or electrical requirements aren't fully specified upfront. Imagine your beautiful built-ins being ready but you forgot to plan for that specific smart device charger or unique pull handle – it can halt everything!

What Can Change the Right Choice:
Often, the complexity of your design, the type of materials you choose, and how quickly approvals happen can significantly impact your timeline. If you're looking for specialty finishes or imported components, those naturally take longer to source and produce. Likewise, if your design involves intricate joinery or integrated lighting, the approval process for shop drawings becomes a critical, time-consuming step.

To keep things running smoothly, it's really important to get detailed shop drawings approved quickly, confirm all dimensions on-site, and make sure every little detail, from hinges to outlets, is accounted for. Revisions after fabrication starts are usually costly and time-consuming. Working with an experienced design-build firm like LineWork Development ensures there's a coordinated process connecting architectural vision and construction expertise, which helps catch these issues early. We aim for a seamless process from the first line to the final detail.
